dosing.evidence: male mice received a 5 mg/kg i.p. injection of racemic 2,5-dimethoxy-4-iodoamphetamine (DOI) or saline

assays.assay_description: Mice were placed in a novel open field environment and allowed to move freely. A 15-min baseline recording was followed by i.p. injection of DOI (5 mg/kg) or saline and a 60-min post-injection recording. Position and velocity were tracked with DeepLabCut to segregate active and rest periods, in synchronization with mPFC electrophysiology recordings.

outcomes.summary: Locomotor velocity was tracked during free exploration of the open field; average velocity (186.26 cm/min) was consistent with non-implanted mice, indicating no overt impairment of locomotion. The open field session was primarily used to segregate active vs. rest behavioral states for neural analysis rather than to test a DOI effect on locomotion per se.
outcomes.evidence: we calculated the average velocity (cm/min) for all male mice during the entire recording session, which we found to be 186.26 cm/min... confirming that our mice exhibit locomotion within a range consistent with that of non-implanted mice.

judge_notes: Qwen returned no assays; glm and gptoss both identified a single Open Field Test assay used to segregate behavioral states for mPFC electrophysiology. Consolidated as one assay.

Although the paper primarily reports electrophysiological outcomes, the rubric scores the behavioural component of behaviour+ephys studies; the OFT (with DeepLabCut tracking and velocity-based active/rest segregation) is the scored behaviour.
B1 scored 2-3 (velocity + active/rest classification = ~2 measures), matching gptoss.
B2 scored No: the paper does not present within-session time-course of behaviour itself; spectrograms are neural data. Overrode glm.
B7 scored Yes due to DeepLabCut pose estimation (head/body/tail markers).
D2 scored 2 (61 min–6 h): continuous 75-min recording session.
